source: Jeff Bezos (1994), Decision Analysis of Amazon Founding; Kahneman (2011), Thinking, Fast and Slow
core_idea: Project yourself to age 80 looking back on your life. Decisions evaluated through this lens minimize path-dependent existential regret rather than short-term social embarrassment, title loss, or temporary discomfort.

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Hesitation driven primarily by immediate fear of social embarrassment or prestige loss rather than fundamental misalignment.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: At age 80, will you regret attempting this and failing more than you would regret never trying and wondering what might have happened?

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Tolerating chronic low-grade dissatisfaction because staying feels passive and safe, even when long-term regret of inaction is near certain.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: If you remain on your current trajectory for 5 more years, what will your cumulative regret look like looking back?

source: Jeff Bezos (1997-2015 Shareholder Letters); Dixit & Pindyck (1994), Investment Under Uncertainty
core_idea: Decisions fall into two categories: Type 1 (one-way doors: irreversible or extremely costly to reverse, requiring slow deliberation) and Type 2 (two-way doors: reversible with low friction, requiring rapid execution).

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Treating a reversible Type 2 experiment as an existential irreversible Type 1 commitment.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: If this move fails completely within 9-12 months, what is the exact economic and professional cost to return to your prior baseline?

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Burning relational bridges or contractual standing during departure, turning an otherwise reversible transition into a permanent lock-out.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: What explicit steps can you take right now to ensure your relationship with current mentors and leadership remains intact?

source: Aswath Damodaran (NYU Stern), Marketability and Illiquidity Discounts in Private Firm Valuation (2005-2023)
core_idea: Private early-stage equity compensation lacks market liquidity and carries heavy seniority liquidation preferences. Rationally, paper startup options must be discounted by 70% to 90% relative to guaranteed liquid cash compensation.

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Treating theoretical fully-diluted paper startup equity valuations as equivalent to liquid cash salary and 401(k) contributions.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: Does this career pivot remain financially viable and personally fulfilling if your startup equity is worth exactly $0 at the end of 4 years?

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Failing to budget for option strike prices and AMT (Alternative Minimum Tax) liabilities upon departure.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: What is the post-termination exercise window, and will you have liquid capital to purchase vested shares if you leave before an IPO/exit?

framework_name: Default Alive vs. Default Dead Runway Analysis
source: Paul Graham (Y Combinator, 2015), 'Default Alive or Default Dead?'
core_idea: A startup is 'Default Alive' if its current revenue growth rate and burn rate allow it to reach profitability before running out of remaining bank balance without raising additional capital.

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Operating under a burn rate where survival is 100% dependent on future venture capital rounds in an uncertain macroeconomic environment.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: If venture capital markets freeze completely for the next 24 months, does your plan reach cashflow break-even on current capital?

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Allocating resources to non-revenue speculative expansions while cash runway is below the 6-month survival threshold.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: What core activities can be paused immediately to extend operating runway past 18 months?

source: Brad Feld & Jason Mendelson (2019), Venture Deals: Be Smarter Than Your Lawyer and Venture Capitalist
core_idea: Preferred investors hold liquidation preferences (1x-3x, participating or non-participating). In modest or moderate acquisition scenarios, preferred capital is returned first, often resulting in common stock receiving near-zero proceeds.

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Assuming common equity shares proportional pro-rata value in low-to-mid exit outcomes without calculating the preferred liquidation hurdle.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: In a $15M or $30M exit, how many dollars of senior preferred capital must be paid out before common shares receive a single dollar?

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Unvetted anti-dilution provisions (full ratchet vs. weighted average) that wipe out founding common equity in subsequent bridge rounds.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: Are your equity protections standard broad-based weighted average, and what veto rights do investors hold over future financings?

source: David Sacks (Craft Ventures, 2020), 'The Burn Multiple: How to Measure Capital Efficiency in SaaS'
core_idea: Burn Multiple = Net Burn / Net New ARR. A score <1.0 is exceptional; 1.0-1.5 is good; >2.0 indicates unsustainable capital subsidization of top-line growth.

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Confusing revenue growth achieved by burning $2.50 per $1.00 of new ARR with genuine organic product-market fit.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: If sales and marketing spend is reduced by 50%, what happens to retention and customer acquisition?

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Customer acquisition cost (CAC) payback period extending beyond 18-24 months without long-term multi-year cash pre-payments.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: Are gross margins sufficient to recover sales acquisition expense within 12 months?

source: Melvin Conway (1968), 'How Do Committees Invent?'; Martin Fowler, Microservice Architecture Patterns
core_idea: Organizations design systems whose architecture mirrors their internal communication channels. Fragmenting code into microservices without organizing autonomous, decoupled teams creates distributed monoliths with high coordination overhead.

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Decomposing into microservices while still requiring simultaneous synchronized deployments across multiple engineers or teams.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: Can service teams deploy independently to production without coordinating pull requests across repositories?

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Replacing in-memory function calls with remote network RPC calls without designing for network partitions, timeouts, and cascading failure.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: What happens to the entire system when the slowest downstream dependency suffers a 5-second latency spike?

source: John Gall (1975), Systemantics: How Systems Work and Especially How They Fail; Joel Spolsky (2000), 'Things You Should Never Do'
core_idea: A complex system that works is invariably found to have evolved from a simple working system. A complex system designed from scratch never works and cannot be patched to make it work.

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Attempting a total clean-slate rewrite of legacy software, underestimating the thousands of edge-case bugfixes encoded in the existing codebase.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: Can this architectural migration be achieved incrementally using the Strangler Fig pattern rather than a binary big-bang cutover?

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Building the new system while the legacy system continues evolving, creating an endless game of feature-parity catch-up.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: Have you locked legacy feature scope, or is the new architecture doomed to chase a moving target?

source: Eric Brewer (2000), CAP Conjecture; Martin Kleppmann (2017), Designing Data-Intensive Applications
core_idea: Under distributed network partitions (P), a storage and database system must choose between strict linearizable Consistency (C) or uninterrupted Availability (A). Claiming both during a partition is structurally impossible.

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Adopting eventual consistency to optimize write throughput without mechanisms to reconcile conflicting asynchronous updates.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: When two conflicting writes occur simultaneously in different regions, what is your deterministic conflict resolution protocol?

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Coupling high-throughput real-time critical paths to transactional relational databases without read-replica caching or rate-limiting.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: If the primary database encounters read lock contention, does the core user flow fail catastrophically or degrade gracefully?

source: Benjamin Graham (1949), The Intelligent Investor; Seth Klarman (1991), Margin of Safety
core_idea: The secret of sound investment is the margin of safety: a significant discount between purchase price and conservatively estimated value, designed to render accurate forecasting unnecessary.

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: A financial or business plan that only breaks even if revenues, occupancy, or market pricing meet 100% of optimistic forecasts.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: If net operating revenues or compensation fall 30% below your baseline projection, can you service all liabilities without distress?

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Evaluating cash yields without reserving 15-25% of gross cashflow for capital expenditures, structural maintenance, and vacancy.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: Have you modeled cash reserves for non-routine capital repairs, legal expenses, and unexpected regulatory compliance costs?

source: John L. Kelly Jr. (1956), 'A New Interpretation of Information Rate'; Edward Thorp (1966), Beat the Dealer
core_idea: The Kelly formula dictates the mathematically optimal fraction of wealth to commit to favorable bets to maximize log-wealth compounding while mathematically reducing the probability of permanent ruin to zero.

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Allocating more than 25-30% of total personal liquid net worth into an illiquid, high-volatility speculative venture or concentrated asset.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: Does a total loss of capital in this single venture impair your ability to meet essential family living expenses and debt payments?

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Assuming edge without factoring estimation error; practical financial engineering mandates betting at 'Fractional Kelly' (half or quarter Kelly).
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: Have you scaled down your committed capital position to buffer against parameter estimation error in your expected payoff?

source: Nassim Nicholas Taleb (2012), Antifragile: Things That Gain from Disorder; Merton Miller (1958), Capital Structure
core_idea: Debt and high fixed operating overhead introduce structural fragility: while they magnify returns on the upside, they transform mild linear revenue declines into non-linear catastrophic default.

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Taking on substantial recurring monthly debt or lease obligations that cannot be downscaled if business conditions deteriorate.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: What percentage of your ongoing costs can be eliminated within 30 days if incoming cashflow contracts by 50%?

diagnostic_checklist.risk_flag: Relying on short-term adjustable debt or balloon payments assuming low interest rates or easy refinancing will always persist.
diagnostic_checklist.probing_question: What is the consequence if interest rates rise 300 basis points when your debt facility or mortgage renews?
